info.title: Sub Rosa account service
info.description: All browser mutations require exact Origin and the session-bound x-csrf-token header matching the subrosa_csrf cookie. Native bearer sessions do not use browser cookies. Cryptographic envelopes are strings containing opaque client ciphertext.

post.summary: Vouch to Carpe Diem that this device may obtain its own key bound to jkt (ADR 0069, ADR 0096). The Carpe Diem key is never returned here
post.description: See docs/carpe-diem-partner-contract.md section 1. The assertion is an ES256 JWS, typ partner-assertion+jwt, valid 120 seconds, carried by the app to the Carpe Diem operator with a DPoP proof from the same ephemeral key. A browser device asks with its browser session and a subrosa-device-proof header bound to jkt; it need not be recent, and its assertion carries kind browser and bound {daily_cap_credits, valid_seconds}. A browser session without a proof answers 403 device_required.

jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the app's ephemeral P-256 key, base64url without padding

403.description: device_required for a browser session, recent_auth_required when the session is older than 300 seconds

404.description: This deployment has no Carpe Diem partner configured

429.description: More than 5 assertions per minute for this account

parameters.name: subrosa-device-proof
parameters.description: Browser devices only. ES256 JWS, typ subrosa-device+jwt, signed by the browser's non-extractable P-256 device key. Claims htm, htu (public URL + path, exact), iat (within 60 s), jti (single use) and, for the assertion, ath = base64url(SHA-256(jkt)). The header carries kid = device id, or jwk = the public key when the device does not exist yet (ADR 0096).

post.summary: Make this browser a device of its account (ADR 0096)
post.description: Browser session with CSRF, authenticated within five minutes. The proof header carries the new device key as jwk. Admission is either a pairing request this browser session created and a live app approved within five minutes (consumed), or recovery_proof, the 32 bytes derived from the recovery key whose SHA-256 the vault holds as admission_verifier. 403 admission_required otherwise, 403 recent_auth_required for an old sign-in, 401 device_proof_invalid for a bad proof, 403 forbidden for an app session or past ten live browser devices.
